subject: Clarify breach-notice matrix and subprocessor jurisdictional impacts
messages:
From: Sofia Rivas <sofia.rivas@novahost.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-11-05T08:12:00-05:00
Subject: Possible exposure reported by customer — need notification timing and evidence scope

Diego,

We received an alert from one of our customers indicating suspicious access to logs that may include tokens issued by your platform. Can you confirm Redwood's notification obligations under our DPA and your subprocessors' jurisdictions? Specifically:

- What is the earliest we would receive a formal breach notice?
- What evidence/export formats are you able to provide (forensic snapshot, telemetry, KMS audit logs)?
- Any cross-border constraints (EU subprocessors, U.S. hosted backups) that will affect transfer speed?

We need to coordinate with our legal and incident response teams — please treat this as time-sensitive. Attaching the customer's initial timeline.

Thx,
Sofia Rivas
Head of Security Programs
Novahost
[Attachment: customer_alert_summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com
To: Sofia Rivas <sofia.rivas@novahost.com>, Megan Liu <megan.liu@novahost.com>
Date: 2025-11-05T10:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Possible exposure reported by customer — need notification timing and evidence scope

Sofia / Megan — thanks for flagging. We take these reports seriously. High level answers up front:

- Notification timing: our DPA (section 7.2) commits to "prompt" notification and a commercially reasonable effort to provide initial notification within 72 hours of confirming a security incident. We often send a preliminary notice earlier if we have high-confidence telemetry.
- Evidence scope: we can provide time-windowed telemetry exports, shard-level request logs, and KMS audit entries. Full forensic snapshots (VM/instance images) are possible but require legal authorization and additional lead time.
- Cross-border constraints: exports from EU subprocessors are subject to data protection local rules. We can export aggregated telemetry quickly; any PII-containing artifacts may require export approvals or redaction, which will add time.

I don't want to overpromise. I'm looping in our privacy and legal leads, plus ops, to confirm what we can commit to and to map a notification matrix specific to Novahost's customer and jurisdictions.

Diego Fernandez
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: DPA_section_7_2_notification_clause.pdf (pdf)]

Diego / team — thanks for the ping. Quick legal assessment and suggested language below.

Observations: our standard DPA language uses "prompt" and "without undue delay" which is flexible. For enterprise customers we have historically agreed to a 72h preliminary notification (subject to confirmation) with a 30-day forensic cooperation window.

Proposed response to Novahost (short):
- We will provide an initial incident notification once Redwood confirms a security incident affecting Novahost, aiming to issue a preliminary notice within 72 hours of confirmation. This notice will include a high-level summary of affected systems and a proposed scope of evidence.
- Forensic evidence: Redwood can provide telemetry exports and KMS audit logs as part of the preliminary package. Full forensic snapshots, if required, will be provided under a documented evidence-handover process and may require export approvals for data originating from EU subprocessors; target time-to-deliver for full snapshot is case-dependent and typically requires up to 14 business days from signed authorization.
- Cross-border: where EU subprocessors are involved we will follow applicable data transfer mechanisms; redaction and legal approvals may be necessary prior to export.

Please review and flag anything I missed. I recommend we offer a single-point escalation contact (Diego) and a mutual action plan (MAP) to formalize timelines.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-11-06T13:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Possible exposure reported by customer — need notification timing and evidence scope

Operational notes from infra:

- We can produce time-bounded telemetry (application logs, request traces) within 24-48 hours for small windows (under 72h of data). Larger windows (days/weeks) may take longer and incur extraction windows.
- KMS audit logs: accessible and exportable without PII; we can provide activity entries within 48 hours.
- Full forensic VM snapshots: need forensic approvals and a temporary snapshot schedule; depending on storage location and legal export constraints (EU-hosted workers), expect 5-15 business days.
- Redaction: automated redaction for PII is limited — we can redact by pattern but cannot guarantee semantic redaction for mixed content. Manual review increases lead time.

I'll attach the current subprocessor roster for reference. If Novahost requires custody transfer/escrow, we will need a DPA addendum and acceptance of a documented handover process.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

Adding privacy POV:

- For anything that contains EU personal data we must check data export mechanisms. If the customer's identity or dataset touches EU residents, we should include conditional language referencing SCCs or other transfer mechanisms and note that additional approvals may be required prior to transfer.
- Evidence custody: recommend we propose a limited-scope evidence handover: (1) preliminary telemetry + KMS events; (2) escrowed forensic snapshot available to Novahost under signed agreement and export approvals.
- Suggested MAP milestone cadence: Initial notice (prelim) within 72 hours of confirmation; preliminary evidence package within 3 business days; formal evidence custody handover process initiation within 5 business days; full snapshot delivery timeline up to 15 business days depending on jurisdiction and redaction needs.

I'll draft the MAP language if you want; Kimberly's suggested clauses look fine.

Laura Bennett
Privacy Lead, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Possible exposure reported by customer — need notification timing and evidence scope (Proposed MAP)

Sofia / team — thank you for the rapid flag and for patience while we lined up internal counsel and ops. Below is a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) to align expectations so your incident response can proceed: 

1) Confirmation & Preliminary Notice (Target: within 72 hours of Redwood confirmation)
   - Redwood will send an initial notification summarizing affected systems, suspected timeline, and immediate mitigations. This will include a high-level assessment of whether EU subprocessors are implicated.

2) Preliminary Evidence Package (Target: by 3 business days after preliminary notice)
   - Included: time-bounded telemetry extracts (application/request traces), KMS audit events, and a list of affected assets. These are CSV/JSON exports.

3) Evidence Handover / Forensic Snapshot (Initiate within 5 business days)
   - If Novahost requests full forensic snapshots, we will require a signed evidence handover agreement. For data originating in EU subprocessors, export approvals or redaction may be needed; estimated delivery 5–15 business days depending on scope.

4) Escalation & Single Point of Contact
   - Redwood SROC contact: Diego Fernandez (diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com). Legal and privacy leads copied.

5) Cross-border Clarification
   - Any transfer of personal data from EU-hosted subprocessors will follow our DPA transfer protocols (SCCs or equivalent). We will highlight any items requiring additional consent or authority before export.

If you agree to the MAP above, we'll prepare a short addendum and initiate the preliminary evidence pull. Please confirm acceptance and any immediate additional evidence fields you need (e.g., specific trace IDs, timeframe).

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
